locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Ongoing Effects, p. 195 (mm3e-heros-handbook#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: effects persist until resisted; dial: the effect description determines what remains during failure; reason: the target has not yet overcome the effect.

rules.statement: A grab can restrain a target after one degree of success or leave it bound after two or more; the grabber is hindered and vulnerable, must spend a free action each turn to maintain the hold, and releases the target if unable to do so.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Grab, pp. 196–197 (mm3e-heros-handbook#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a successful hold restricts the target’s movement and defenses; dial: stronger success increases restriction, while maintaining it occupies the grabber and uses a limb; reason: holding someone requires continued effort.

rules.statement: A grabber can drag a restrained or bound target, but the target gets a Strength resistance check; on failure the target moves along, while success leaves the grabber immobilized for the turn unless the hold is released.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Grab, p. 197 (mm3e-heros-handbook#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the holder may move a captured target; dial: resistance can stop the movement and immobilize the holder; reason: the target can fight the pull.

rules.statement: A character recovering during a conflict may remove their highest damage or fatigue level, or make an extra resistance check against an ongoing effect; this can be done only once per conflict and grants +2 to active defenses until the next turn begins.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Recover, pp. 197–198 (mm3e-heros-handbook#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recovery trades the whole turn for a limited respite; dial: choose between clearing a condition or trying to end an ongoing effect; reason: the character must pause to regain composure.

rules.statement: Attackers can combine attacks only when they share an effect and resistance and are within 5 ranks; they delay to the slowest attacker’s initiative, and successful additional attacks add +2 to the strongest attack’s rank for one degree of success or +5 for three or more.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Team Attacks, p. 200 (mm3e-heros-handbook#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: compatible attacks can reinforce one another; dial: matching effect, resistance, rank proximity, and coordinated timing limit combinations; reason: attackers must synchronize similar effects.

rules.statement: A charging attacker may use movement rank or normal damage rank plus 1, whichever is higher, and gains a further +1 after moving full speed; the attacker then resists half the attack’s damage rank, rounded down.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Slam Attack, pp. 199–200 (mm3e-heros-handbook#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: momentum increases attack impact; dial: the attacker risks taking half the attack’s damage; reason: collision force affects both participants.

rules.statement: A player can attempt an unusual stunt outside the hero’s normal abilities by spending a hero point; this cost permits the attempt but does not itself guarantee success. Alternatively, the GM can treat an unusual feat as extra effort.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Page 206, Saying Yes to Your Players (mm3e-heros-handbook#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep attempts within established abilities; dial: allow broader stunts for a hero-point or extra-effort cost, because extraordinary acts should be occasional.

rules.statement: The GM can award at least 1 hero point for each scene before an adventure’s finale, and can award more by introducing additional complications. The GM should generally give different heroes’ complications roughly equal opportunities to earn points over one adventure or, if needed, two or three.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Page 211, Awarding Hero Points (mm3e-heros-handbook#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: roughly one point per pre-finale scene; dial: increase points by adding complications, because setbacks provide resources for later challenges.

rules.statement: For a completed adventure that lasts one session, each hero generally gains 1 power point; especially difficult adventures can yield 2. Longer adventures generally grant 1 additional point per session, with a possible 1- or 2-point completion bonus; the GM may vary or withhold awards.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Pages 211–212, Awarding Power Points (mm3e-heros-handbook#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: modest advancement for completion and session length; dial: change or withhold awards to match the series’ pace and how successfully the heroes dealt with the adventure.

rules.statement: Between adventures, players can spend awarded power points to improve traits, subject to the series power-level limit, or save them until that limit rises. When heroes have accumulated about 15 additional points since the series began or its last power-level increase, the GM should consider raising the limit by 1; a slower pace of 20, 30, or more points, or no further increases, is also permitted.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Pages 211–212, Awarding Power Points; Increasing Power Level (mm3e-heros-handbook#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: improve traits within the current limit and consider a one-level increase at 15 earned points; dial: raise the threshold or freeze the limit to encourage broader development.

rules.statement: A device intended to become a regular part of a hero’s abilities generally must be paid for with earned power points; the GM can require points to be set aside or future awards to go toward its cost. A one-time use of a captured device can instead cost 1 hero point, as with a stunt or invention.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Page 212, Equipment (mm3e-heros-handbook#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permanent equipment costs advancement points; dial: permit a temporary use for a hero point, because captured technology may be usable without becoming a lasting ability.

rules.statement: The GM can make damage more lethal by having an attack that incapacitates its target also make the target dying. Other options include treating a minion’s defeat as death, or making specified attack types always use this lethal rule.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Page 207, Going for the Kill (mm3e-heros-handbook#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: incapacitation does not itself make a target dying; dial: apply the lethal option to chosen attacks or targets, because the series may portray greater danger.

rules.statement: A further optional lethality rule makes four or more degrees of failure on a resistance check against Damage—or an Affliction that can cause dying—cause immediate death. Another option slows recovery from conditions caused by a killing attack to one condition per hour or per day.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Page 207, Going for the Kill (mm3e-heros-handbook#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: no immediate death from this failure threshold and ordinary recovery; dial: impose the harsh death rule or slower recovery to make lethal attacks more consequential.

rules.statement: When the GM allows heroes to keep equipment supplied by a patron, the GM decides whether it requires power-point expenditure or is free in point cost; patron support may carry future complications or other strings.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Page 212, Wealth; Equipment (mm3e-heros-handbook#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the GM sets whether sponsored resources cost points; dial: attach conditions or future complications because outside support may come with obligations.

rules.statement: A campaign spanning multiple realities requires some means of traveling between dimensions; choosing a smaller geographic scope makes places easier for players to learn, while a larger scope supports greater threats, including danger to whole worlds.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Scale (p. 214) (mm3e-heros-handbook#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the campaign’s scale consistent; dial: widen it to enable interdimensional travel and world-scale stakes.

rules.statement: A character asleep is defenseless, stunned, and unaware. A hearing Perception check with at least three degrees of success, sudden movement such as shaking, or an effect that permits a resistance check wakes the character and removes those conditions.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Glossary (p. 220) (mm3e-heros-handbook#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sleep sharply limits action and awareness; dial: allow more reliable waking only through specified stimuli or a successful hearing check.

rules.statement: A character directed by an outside force while still resisting is limited to free actions and one standard action per turn, and the controller chooses both; that standard action may be traded for a move action. Full control overrides this lesser state.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Glossary (p. 220) (mm3e-heros-handbook#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: outside direction limits agency; dial: stronger control removes the target’s remaining choice.

rules.statement: An effect can counter another by making an opposed power check; ordinarily this takes a readied action, but spending a hero point allows an immediate reaction instead.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Glossary (p. 221) (mm3e-heros-handbook#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: countering costs preparation and an action; dial: permit immediate intervention at the cost of a hero point.

rules.statement: A critical hit normally adds 5 damage, but the attacker may instead add an effect or use an alternate effect.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Glossary (p. 221) (mm3e-heros-handbook#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a critical hit increases harm; dial: exchange that increase for a different effect.

rules.statement: An incapacitated character is defenseless, stunned, and unaware, and generally falls prone unless something keeps them standing.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Glossary (p. 222) (mm3e-heros-handbook#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: incapacitation removes action and awareness; dial: external support can prevent the fall but not the other limitations.

rules.statement: Effects have five durations: instant effects occur and end in the same turn; concentration effects require a standard action each round to maintain; sustained effects require a free action each round; continuous and permanent effects need no maintenance, but permanent effects cannot be switched off.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Glossary (p. 221) (mm3e-heros-handbook#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: duration determines upkeep and whether an effect can be ended; dial: longer-lasting effects reduce maintenance but may sacrifice control.

rules.statement: A dying character immediately makes a Fortitude check against DC 15. Success has no further result, two degrees of success stabilize the character, and three total degrees of failure cause death; checks repeat each round until death or stabilization, while a successful DC 15 Treatment check or Healing effect from another character stabilizes them.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Glossary (p. 221) (mm3e-heros-handbook#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dying risks death over repeated checks; dial: provide aid to stabilize, while the check thresholds set the danger.

rules.statement: A transformed character may have appearance or traits changed, including traits removed and others added, but the transformation cannot increase the character’s power-point total; it may reduce that total for its duration.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Glossary (p. 223) (mm3e-heros-handbook#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation may alter traits but cannot grant a larger total; dial: permit temporary loss of capability as the cost of the change.

rules.statement: A character with total visual concealment is harder to target: concealment gives a –2 attack-check penalty when partial and –5 when total. A character without sight treats everything as having full visual concealment and is hindered, visually unaware, and vulnerable.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Glossary (pp. 220–221) (mm3e-heros-handbook#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: impaired visibility hinders targeting and other visual tasks; dial: partial versus total concealment sets the severity.

rules.statement: While vulnerable, a character’s active defenses are halved, rounding the final value up. If the character is also defenseless, that condition takes precedence.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Vulnerable (p. 223) (mm3e-heros-handbook#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the defense reduction while the condition lasts; dial: none, since the passage gives no way to resist or end it.

rules.statement: Weakened means a character has temporarily lost power points from one trait; debilitated takes precedence if both conditions apply.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Weakened (p. 223) (mm3e-heros-handbook#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the trait loss is temporary; dial: none, as the passage does not specify its amount or recovery timing.

rules.statement: Each rank step above rank 0 doubles the listed mass, time, distance, and volume measures; each step below halves them. The table gives, for example, rank 0 as 24 kg, 6 seconds, 8 m, and .025 m³, and rank 1 as 50 kg, 12 seconds, 16 m, and .05 m³.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Measurements Table: Metric (p. 225) (mm3e-heros-handbook#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed rank measures; dial: none, since the progression sets a scale rather than a power cost.

rules.statement: Size rank changes listed traits: larger ranks reduce active defense and stealth while increasing intimidation, Strength, Stamina, and sometimes speed; smaller ranks apply the reverse modifiers shown in the table. For example, size rank 1 gives –6 active defense, –12 stealth, +6 intimidation, +12 Strength, +12 Stamina, and +1 speed.
locators: M&M 3e Hero's Handbook: Size Rank Modifiers (p. 225) (mm3e-heros-handbook#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the table’s modifiers for the character’s size; dial: none, because the passage specifies effects but no transformation cost.
